title: a wrong-length literal in the right operand of or, after a variable that holds True, runs at -O1 and above and is rejected at -O0
compiler: prints `True` at -O1, -O2 and -O3, the default, and with mojo run and -D ASSERT=all; -O0 rejects it with "function instantiation failed" and the note "constraint failed: expected 1 elements in the SIMD list literal, found 3". The comparison alone, and the same or with `var t = False`, are rejected at every level
fixed: rejects it at every level, as -O0 does and as every level rejects the comparison alone (noMatchingInit)

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular. 2026-11-26, the human: "Isn't this a shortcut or like C has? But maybe it is not a compiler bug - still worth me checking with mojo people." Four cases to raise with Modular, each run on the pin (#346), where the comparison alone is rejected at every level: (1) `var t = True; print(t or ([1] != [[1, 2, 3]]))` prints `True` at -O1, -O2 and -O3, the default, and -O0 rejects it with "constraint failed: expected 1 elements in the SIMD list literal, found 3"; (2) `var t = False; print(t and ([1] != [[1, 2, 3]]))` prints `False` at -O1, -O2 and -O3, and -O0 rejects it with the same constraint; (3) the dead `if` branch `var t = True; if t: print(1) else: print([1] != [[1, 2, 3]])` prints `1` at -O1, -O2 and -O3, and -O0 rejects it with the same constraint; (4) the literal `print(True or ([1] != [[1, 2, 3]]))` prints `True` at every level, -O0 included, with the warning "unreachable code on right side of 'True or ...'". The question for Modular is whether an or/and operand that is never evaluated is meant to be type-checked and instantiated.

nightly.result: checked on the pin only; no newer nightly was run
